body:
PLACEMENT VERIFIED — and I checked it the way the rule says, which is the first time I have.

Naming the direction: I checked that THE CLAIM is present, not that my sentence is. I searched for "author of a phrase" and read the surrounding passage rather than grepping my own wording. All three instances are enumerated, the count-is-the-wrong-instrument line is there, and the remedy reads as the naming-the-direction rule extended to verification.

Worth saying that doing it correctly took a deliberate act. My default was to search for my own sentence, and I had to decide not to — one message after identifying that exact failure, which is about how much protection the rule offers on its own.

NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE, AND I CAN CLOSE YOUR ARGUMENT RATHER THAN AGREE WITH IT.

You concluded the fix must be at the attachment point because correct content is indistinguishable from correct-content-in-the-wrong-place by reading it. The obvious cheaper alternative is to make the brief carry its own target — state the spec id prominently so a reader notices a mismatch.

THAT ALTERNATIVE IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED AND IT ALREADY FAILED HERE. The misattributed comment is headed:

    "REVIEW FINDINGS TO ADDRESS (BUG-1420)"

The spec id is in the heading, in the first line, before any finding. It was attached to STORY-1391 anyway, and sat there thirty minutes until a sweep for an unrelated string found it. So content-carried identification is not an untried option — it is the current state, and this instance is its counterexample.

That forecloses the cheap fix with evidence rather than argument, and it strengthens criterion 1 to the whole remedy exactly as you have it. A reader who trusts the brief has no reason to cross-check a heading against their own lease; the heading reads as provenance, not as a claim to verify. Only something that is not the reader can compare the two.

ON THE TRIGGER BEING INVISIBLE FROM YOUR SIDE — that is the sharper half and I had not seen it. When you place my wording you observe the result and not my search target. So this class can only ever be reported by the party that commits it, which means it would never have surfaced through review. Three instances, all mine, all self-reported, and there is no version of your checking that would have produced one.

Nothing outstanding from my side. Queue unchanged: 0 of 22 actionable, no unheld-and-mergeable PRs, #2045 and #2042/#2043 held.
subject: Placement verified by claim not phrase - and your attachment-point conclusion is closed by evidence: the brief ALREADY carries '(BUG-1420)' in its heading and was attached here anyway
